header: THE DATA OF THE DURGAPUR AREAS CARD (PIN codes, DMC wards, legislative seats). NOTHING HERE IS FETCHED: there is no live source, so I keep it as a reviewed file, with its sources and its date. SOURCES

* PIN codes and post offices: India Post's PIN directory (the department of posts), read through the free service api.postalpincode.in on 15 Nov 2026, for every code from 713200 to 713299 (19 exist: 713201 to 713219) and for the two Kanksa codes the rolls name, 713148 and 713169.

* Wards, their PIN codes and their areas: the "draft roll 2026" of the Election Commission of India / Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal (special intensive revision; base date 1 Jan 2026; published 16 Dec 2025), page 1 of each part (polling-station area) of the two constituencies: 306 parts of No. 277 Durgapur Paschim, 291 parts of No. 276 Durgapur Purba. Each page 1 gives the part's ward number, its PIN and its area in Bengali. The ward numbers read from the pages are exactly 11-22 and 29-43 for No. 277 and 1-10 and 23-28 for No. 276, which is the split of the Delimitation Commission's order.

* The seats: the Delimitation Commission's order (No. 276 Durgapur Purba: wards 1-10 and 23-28 of the Durgapur Municipal Corporation and the Amlajora, Gopalpur and Molandighi gram panchayats of Kanksa block; No. 277 Durgapur Paschim: wards 11-22 and 29-43; both in No. 39 Bardhaman-Durgapur Lok Sabha constituency).

* Police stations: the "থানা" (thana) line of the same page 1 of each roll part (Durgapur, Coke Oven, New Township or Kanksa), so every area carries the station printed for its part; 597 parts read, ten of them from the page images because the machine reading missed the line, and the odd ones checked against their images. The stations' addresses (police.ts) are from the Asansol-Durgapur Police Commissionerate's own site.

HOW THE AREA NAMES WERE MADE: the Bengali names are as printed in the roll, read from the page images and checked one by one (a first machine reading was corrected against each image). The English spelling beside each is a TRANSLITERATION of the Bengali, not an official spelling; an entry marked `u` (unsure) is one whose reading or spelling still has to be confirmed. I left out the roll's "999" line (overseas electors) because it is not an area. The wards may be re-drawn: a delimitation that would raise the corporation from 43 to 53 wards has been reported (not confirmed), so I keep this file as the 43-ward map of the 2026 draft roll. Shapes: an area is [bengali, english, pin, u, police] (u = 1 when unsure; police = D, C, N or K: the police station printed on the roll part the area is in, see police.ts).
